questions.q: Which three points in a data's lifecycle does this lesson identify as needing encryption?
options: At creation, at deletion, and at backup only
Only at rest — the other two don't apply to databases
Only in transit — data at rest never needs protection
At rest, in transit, and in use
questions.explain: The lesson covers data sitting on disk (at rest), moving across a network (in transit, via TLS), and being actively processed in memory (in use).

questions.q: In the TDE key chain shown in this lesson, what does the master key protect?
options: The symmetric key used for cell-level encryption only
The certificate, which in turn protects the database encryption key
Nothing — the master key is only used for login authentication
The data pages directly, with no certificate involved
questions.explain: The chain is: master key protects the certificate, the certificate protects the database encryption key, and the database encryption key encrypts the actual data pages.

questions.q: Which T-SQL functions does this lesson use to perform cell-level encryption and decryption of a single column?
options: ANONYMIZE and DEANONYMIZE
ENCRYPTBYKEY and DECRYPTBYKEY
MASKED WITH and UNMASK
TOKENIZE and DETOKENIZE
questions.explain: ENCRYPTBYKEY writes ciphertext into a column using an open symmetric key, and DECRYPTBYKEY reverses it back to the original value.

questions.q: What specific problem does Always Encrypted solve that TDE and cell-level encryption do not, per this lesson?
options: It automatically masks all columns in a table by default
It makes the database faster to query than an unencrypted database
It removes the need for any key management at all
It prevents even a database administrator with sysadmin access from seeing plaintext, since decryption happens at the client driver, outside the engine
questions.explain: TDE and cell-level encryption both decrypt inside the database engine, so a sufficiently privileged DBA can still see plaintext; Always Encrypted moves that boundary to the client driver so the engine itself never holds the key or plaintext.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stress backing up the TDE certificate and its private key immediately after creating it?
options: The certificate is only needed for cell-level encryption, not TDE
The certificate expires automatically after 24 hours if not backed up
Without that certificate, an encrypted database and its backups become permanently unreadable, even to the organization that encrypted them
SQL Server requires a backup before ALTER DATABASE SET ENCRYPTION ON will run at all
questions.explain: The certificate protects the database encryption key in the TDE chain; losing it means losing the ability to ever decrypt the database or its backups again.
